teams.heading: Jake White emerges as favourite to be named new Fiji coach
teams.body: Former Springboks boss Jake White has emerged as the favourite to become Fiji's next head coach, ahead of fellow applicant Warren Gatland. The Fiji Rugby Union has reportedly shortlisted candidates after receiving 31 applications to succeed Mick Byrne, who stepped down in April. White, who led South Africa to World Cup glory in 2007, is regarded as the leading candidate for a role starting immediately and running until the end of 2027.

lead.why: Jake White has emerged as the frontrunner for the vacant Fiji head coach job ahead of Warren Gatland.

teams.heading: France held the world number one ranking for one week
teams.body: France's longest unbroken spell at No. 1 in the world rankings is one week. This single week at the top of the official rankings occurred from July 2022 to July 2022. Les Bleus have not managed to put together a longer consecutive run at the top of the global standings during any other period. No other French team has exceeded this seven-day stint at the summit.

teams.heading: Ireland women seal consecutive victories over Japan with seven-try Cork display
teams.body: The Ireland women’s national side built crucial momentum ahead of their WXV campaign with a comprehensive 43-19 victory over Japan on Saturday. After recovering from an early Japanese try at Virgin Media Park, the hosts crossed four times in the first half to secure a 22-7 lead. Beibhinn Parsons extended her national try-scoring record to 25 before debutants Alana McInerney and Sophie Barrett both scored off the bench. Scott Bemand’s side now head to South Africa having won consecutive autumn fixtures.

lead.why: The national side's comprehensive seven-try victory over Japan in Cork is the weekend's major international result.

teams.heading: Josh Adams targets third World Cup after declaring fitness for Wales
teams.body: Josh Adams has declared himself on track for Wales' November internationals after overcoming a calf injury. The 31-year-old Cardiff wing, who has played 72 internationals, missed the summer tour defeat to South Africa and the start of the domestic season. However, Adams expects to make his club comeback this month before joining the national squad. He also confirmed his desire to represent Wales at next year's World Cup in Australia.

teams.heading: Les Kiss forced into midfield reshuffle as Hunter Paisami receives four-match suspension
teams.body: Australia head coach Les Kiss is considering his midfield options for the upcoming Bledisloe Cup tests after Hunter Paisami was handed a four-match ban. The centre was suspended following a dangerous tackle during the recent test against South Africa in Perth. While Kiss is reportedly frustrated by the length of the ruling, he has remained coy about who will fill the vacancy in the midfield. The disciplinary blow forces a selection rethink as the Wallabies look to build on their recent 57-10 victory over Italy.

teams.heading: Rennie confirms Ruben Love will miss remainder of 2026 international season
teams.body: All Blacks fly-half Ruben Love has been ruled out for the remainder of the international season. An official statement confirmed that "Ruben Love will undergo surgery after sustaining an ankle ligament injury", a blow for the playmaker who established himself as Dave Rennie’s first-choice No. 10 this year. With Love sidelined for upcoming Nations Championship fixtures, Rennie has named Richie Mo'unga and Josh Jacomb in the squad, while Beauden Barrett and Damian McKenzie provide further specialist cover.

lead.why: It is an exclusive report regarding a season-ending surgery for the team's breakout first-choice fly-half.

teams.heading: Dave Rennie continues to challenge Springboks' scrum and aerial tactics
teams.body: All Blacks head coach Dave Rennie has confirmed he will continue to lobby World Rugby regarding South Africa's scrummaging and aerial game. Rennie claims the Springboks’ tightheads gain an illegal advantage by angling in and “walking sideways” during set-pieces. He also questioned the effectiveness of the current brake foot law. Regarding the aerial battle, Rennie insisted that New Zealand would persist with their high-ball tactics despite admitting the Boks gained a “major advantage” in that area during their recent head-to-head encounters.

lead.why: It addresses the ongoing tactical friction between the Springboks and the All Blacks regarding scrum and aerial play.
